title: Patterns in Noise
objective: After this level you can spot the Texas sharpshooter fallacy: drawing the target around the bullet holes after the fact.
summary: The Texas sharpshooter draws the target after shooting, making chance look like skill. Cancer cluster investigators guard against it by setting their definitions first.

cards.headline: Fire at a barn, then paint the bull's-eye around the holes. Great shot?
cards.body: Every shot is a bull's-eye if you draw the target afterward. That picture gave its name to a real reasoning error, the Texas sharpshooter fallacy, and it hides wherever people go looking for patterns after the fact.

cards.headline: Targets drawn afterward
cards.body: The Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy says the fallacy comes from overemphasizing random results, or making selective use of coincidence. Its example: Psychic Sarah makes 26 predictions for the year. When one of them comes true, she says she can see into the future. The misses quietly vanish, and the one hit becomes the bull's-eye.

cards.headline: Clusters that aren't
cards.body: Cancer is common, so cases can appear to cluster even when they have no connection at all. That's why CDC guidance warns investigators about the Texas sharpshooter: notice the cases first, then draw the "affected" area around them, and a link appears that may be nothing but chance. In one review of US cancer cluster investigations over 20 years, a clear cause turned up in just one case.

cards.headline: Draw the target first
cards.body: The same CDC guidance gives the cure: investigators must set out their definitions, assumptions and methods before they look. The habit works anywhere. Decide what counts as a hit before the evidence comes in. Think your lucky socks win games? Pick the games you'll count before the season starts, not after the wins.

mascot.line: Keep this: decide what counts as a hit before you look, never after.

cards.headline: The sharpshooter: spotted
learned: The sharpshooter draws the target after shooting
Chance plus hindsight looks like a pattern
Decide what counts as a hit before you look

questions.prompt: Match each part of the sharpshooter lesson with its partner on the cards.

pairs.right: Paint the bull's-eye around the holes

questions.explanation: The Texas sharpshooter fires first, then paints the bull's-eye around the holes. Psychic Sarah made 26 predictions. CDC guidance says to set out definitions, assumptions and methods before looking.

questions.prompt: Why can drawing a cluster's boundary after spotting the cases create a false link?

options.label: Maps are always inaccurate
options.rationale: The maps are fine; the timing of the boundary is the flaw.

options.label: The area is chosen to fit the cases
Cancer never clusters for real
options.rationale: The point is chance clusters, not that real ones can't exist.

options.label: Investigators always ignore the cases
options.rationale: The problem is drawing around them, not ignoring them.

questions.explanation: Cases of a common disease can cluster by chance; drawing the area around them afterward makes that chance look like a link.

questions.prompt: Psychic Sarah's forgotten misses play the same role as what in Bacon's temple story?

options.label: The sailors who survived
options.rationale: Those are the hits on the wall.

options.label: The paintings on the wall
options.rationale: The paintings show hits, not misses.

options.label: The visitor asking questions
options.rationale: He's the one pointing at the misses.

options.label: The sailors who prayed and drowned

questions.explanation: Both stories count the hits and let the misses vanish: Sarah's failed predictions, Bacon's drowned sailors.
